title: Next New Moon Calculator: Dark-Sky Dates
description: Find the date of the next new moon with the Next New Moon Calculator — the darkest nights for stargazing, by the 29.53-day cycle. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, after the full moon of October 26, 2026, the next new moon falls on November 9, 2026 — the night the Milky Way gets the sky to itself.
quick_answer: The Next New Moon Calculator finds the date of the next new moon after today or any date you enter, counted on the Moon's 29.53-day cycle. Enter a date and learn when the Moon goes dark — the anchor date for stargazing trips, lunar calendars and spring-tide planning.

body.t: Deep-sky nights are planned backwards from new moon — the
Months in lunar calendars (and festivals keyed to them) begin at new moon — this is the reference date.
Solar eclipses happen only at new moon — the calculator finds the candidate dates the eclipse maps then refine.
Spring tides ride new moons too; night anglers plan the dark-plus-tide combination starting here.
Full moon October 26, 2026 → new moon November 9, 2026: 14 days of waning. The cycle's halves are as regular as its whole.
At new moon the Moon sits between Earth and Sun: its lit half faces away and it rises and sets with the Sun. The darkest night is a geometry fact, not a mood.

faq: By counting the mean 29.53-day synodic cycle from a known new moon — within hours for planning purposes, which is all a dark night needs.
Is the new moon night completely dark?
Moonlight-wise, yes — the Moon is up only in daytime. Starlight, airglow and light pollution remain, as every rural camper learns.
When is the best stargazing window?
The three or four nights centred on new moon, before the waxing crescent starts competing after sunset.
Lunar months (29 or 30 days alternating) chase this cycle; the Gregorian calendar ignores it, which is why full moons drift through the month.
Can a month have no new moon?
February can — it is shorter than the cycle, so a new moon can slip from late January to early March (last in 2014, a curiosity the calculator reproduces).
